runners_data.name: Shadow Brigade
runners_data.note: Trainer George Scott has a solid 3/14 strike rate over the past fortnight and Darragh Keenan is a competent booking, but Shadow Brigade's natural instinct is to race from the rear — it is only on the lead here because the field lacks a genuine front runner, and racing outside its comfort zone at 138lbs is a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Brighton View
runners_data.note: William Knight's yard is in decent form at 4/18 over 14 days, and Brighton View brings a legitimate course-trip profile with a win at 10f on good ground in its history and sim-going form reading three from six with a winner and two places — Marco Ghiani should be able to time a run from this small field.

runners_data.name: Mr Bollinger
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane, one of the most electric finishing riders in the country, suits a horse that wants to come late, and Mr Bollinger's recent 12f win on good ground is the most relevant piece of form here — mapped to midfield but genuinely a hold-up horse, so expect it to be last into the straight before Loughnane asks it to quicken.

races.paceDynamic: Shadow Brigade is the only confirmed pace-setter in this three-runner field, though its true style is hold-up — it has been redistributed to the front because no genuine front runner exists and someone must set the gallop. With just three runners over 1m3½f on good-to-firm turf at Yarmouth, Shadow Brigade is likely to drift forward and establish a steady, uncontested lead, creating a controlled tempo with minimal pressure. Brighton View and Mr Bollinger are both natural hold-up types, meaning the pace is almost certain to be modest and the race will be decided by who picks up most cleanly from off the pace in the straight. This shape strongly favours horses with a late turn of foot and the ability to accelerate on a flat, galloping track — a waiting game that rewards quality of finish over positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow pace, sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Brigade drifts to the front and sets a gentle gallop, turning the race into a tactical crawl.
scenarios.body: With the tempo compressed over the final two furlongs, the winner will be whoever quickens sharpest off the steady pace — Brighton View's strong recent form at this trip and going positions it well for this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Shadow Brigade dictates, holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Shadow Brigade, racing out of its natural role, finds the lead comfortable and builds an unassailable advantage.
scenarios.body: Uncontested and relaxed in front, Shadow Brigade could exploit the minimal pressure and simply refuse to be caught if its rivals leave it alone too long.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mr Bollinger times run late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that Mr Bollinger can sit last and unleash a telling finish from off the back.
scenarios.body: Mr Bollinger's recent win over 12f on good ground shows it can finish strongly at a staying trip, and Billy Loughnane's big-race instincts could engineer a well-timed run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested early, strong stayer wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three runners jostle for position early, injecting enough pace to stretch the field and suit the most genuine stayer.
scenarios.body: An uncharacteristically honest gallop would sap the finish from the more sprint-reliant horses, rewarding whichever runner handles the test of stamina best over the 1m3½f.

watchPoints.text: Shadow Brigade is racing entirely out of role at the front — if it fails to settle and wastes energy fighting for a position it doesn't want, it could stop quickly in the straight.

With only three runners, Brighton View and Mr Bollinger could both sit motionless behind Shadow Brigade, creating a genuine dawdle — watch for the pace to be so slow that the first furlong splits are misleadingly tight.

Mr Bollinger is tagged with a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 racing out of role — if the race is run to suit a true hold-up horse, its chances improve, but Loughnane must judge the pace correctly from a midfield map position that doesn't reflect the horse's natural pattern.

Going recorded as Good to Firm for this race — all three runners are marked OK for the going, but the fast surface on Yarmouth's flat track will accentuate any difference in finishing speed, making the sprint-finish scenario the dominant frame for this race.

runners_data.name: Aspire To Glory
runners_data.note: Chronically out of form (six runs without a placing on similar ground), Tom Marquand's booking is a mild positive but this horse's natural front-running instincts are likely to be suppressed in a field already crowded for prominent berths, reducing her effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Nicely Curved
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who showed placed form on good ground earlier this season; Jonny Peate takes over for Hayley Burton with the yard showing a narrow recent strike rate, and 36 days between runs adds a fitness query, but her style is authentic and she is the truest closer in the race.

runners_data.name: Oh So Audacious
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner — 14 of 15 career runs on similar ground with 2 wins and 7 places — Kaiya Fraser takes over in a yard with a cold 14-day record, but this horse's course affinity and uncontested lead make her the dominant pace shape beneficiary.

runners_data.name: Valsharah
runners_data.note: Four-day turnaround for Michael Appleby, who is adept at running horses back quickly; multiple placed efforts on good ground at 6-7f suggest the trip and conditions suit, and Harry Davies is a strong booking — she is the most likely horse to press Oh So Audacious and benefit if the leader tires.

runners_data.name: Caitlin G
runners_data.note: The ⚠ fade flag is significant — Grace McEntee has little to work with on a horse that has placed just once in five runs over suitable trips on good ground, and a 3-year-old against older rivals with a tendency to weaken late makes her a marginal player in most shapes.

runners_data.name: Girls Allowed
runners_data.note: Natural prominent type who is unlikely to secure her preferred position with Oh So Audacious and Valsharah already filling that space; a 53-day absence for a yard without a recent win, combined with the positional compromise, means this race shape works against her natural rhythm.

races.paceDynamic: Oh So Audacious is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no horse genuinely capable of matching her early, she should establish a comfortable lead at a sustainable gallop on this flat Yarmouth 7f. Valsharah will likely press from a prominent position, giving Oh So Audacious some company without genuinely testing her, while Aspire To Glory and Girls Allowed — both natural prominent types — are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield role as there simply is not room for all of them to race where they want. The field holds more prominent/front-running types than can realistically secure that position, with Oh So Audacious best placed to dictate and Valsharah the most likely to actually land close-up cover. An unhurried, controlled gallop on good-to-firm ground over 7f strongly favours horses who can sit handy and quicken off the pace — true hold-up horses like Nicely Curved and Caitlin G will need the pace to be genuine to land a blow late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If Oh So Audacious sets an uncontested, even gallop and kicks on turning for home.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard, conserving energy through a sustainable fractions before asserting in the final two furlongs; her excellent course form at Yarmouth on good ground makes this her optimum shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Valsharah and Aspire To Glory push forward early, heating up the early pace.
scenarios.body: A more contested early fractions puts pressure on Oh So Audacious and opens the door for the horses sitting just off the pace; Valsharah, already comfortable on this going with multiple placed efforts, is well suited to a contested but honest gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a strong enough gallop that they tie up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Nicely Curved, a genuine hold-up type with proven placed form on good ground, would be the main beneficiary as she times her run from off the pace; Caitlin G's tendency to fade limits her claims even in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems and positional scrapping between the redistributed prominent types cause a chaotic early race.
scenarios.body: Girls Allowed, forced wide or into an unnatural position, could capitalise if she threads through a scrambled field at the death; the lack of genuine form at this level and on this track makes it a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Oh So Audacious's ability to steal an uncontested lead unchallenged is the defining factor — watch whether Valsharah or Aspire To Glory push forward to press her in the first two furlongs, as that changes the shape entirely.

Aspire To Glory and Girls Allowed are both naturally prominent types forced into midfield — if either horse's jockey fights for position in the early stages, the gallop could quicken sharply and unsettle the entire field.

Nicely Curved's 36-day absence is worth watching in the paddock — if she looks fresh and well, her hold-up style becomes more credible late; if she appears ring-rusty early, she may never land a blow.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this 7f race — the fast surface rewards horses with a fluent action who travel well into their races, which suits Valsharah's consistent placed form on this ground more than the hold-up horses needing late cut.

races.name: Bodhi Solutions - Constructing Champions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Daretobedifferent
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good going 23 days ago in good form, but a natural hold-up horse thrust into the role of likely pace-setter here; Marco Ghiani is an experienced rider who may make the best of the position, though the horse is racing fully out of character and a style discount applies.

runners_data.name: Okiru
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand's booking for Archie Watson is noteworthy; ran a solid second over 7f on Good to Firm and fourth over 8f Good recently, and while a true hold-up type, has the pace profile to sit midfield and quicken in a small compressed field — blinkers removed (hg:b) worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Melting Snow
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop sends this hold-up horse in a first-time hood (hg:p) which often signals an intended step forward; has been running consistently 4th-8th at slightly longer trips and shorter, and Billy Loughnane's booking is a positive, though the horse's genuine rear-running style means it needs a stronger-than-likely pace to be seen to best advantage.

runners_data.name: Guest House
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa riding, with a striking course-and-going profile of 8 runs on Good at Yarmouth producing a win and three places — the most course-relevant CV in the field; a hold-up horse by nature but well-placed by the redistribution to track the pace, and recent return to form (1st ten days ago) makes it live.

runners_data.name: Bellini Spirit
runners_data.note: John & Thys Flint's yard is 3/8 in 14 days so in form, but Bellini Spirit hasn't run for 86 days — the longest layoff in the field — and its recent form on Soft and Standard ground with a poor 18th last time on Good is a significant concern; a true hold-up type mapped to midfield with limited evidence this trip or going suits.

runners_data.name: Esdaile
runners_data.note: James Tate's runner, 12 days since last run, has four consecutive finishes outside the top five including 10th, 6th, 10th on his last four starts; a hold-up horse by profile and the lowest-rated in the field, facing a stiff task to reverse recent declining form even in a forgiving small-field race.

races.paceDynamic: Daretobedifferent is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this six-runner 1m Yarmouth handicap on Good to Firm ground, redistributed to the lead as the most likely pace-maker despite a natural hold-up profile, meaning the fractions are likely to be measured and controlled rather than pressured. With no genuine front-running rival to force an honest gallop, the tempo should be modest and the race could develop into a tactical crawl before a sprint finish in the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Melting Snow, Guest House, Bellini Spirit, and Esdaile are all true hold-up horses shown in midfield, and Guest House or Melting Snow, both placed previously from similar positions, are most likely to secure the better tracking positions behind the sole leader. This shape strongly favours horses that can sit close to a slow pace and quicken, rather than those waiting from the rear, as a steady gallop on Good to Firm turf at Yarmouth's flat, undemanding track will not generate enough momentum to bring late closers into the race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Tracking Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Daretobedifferent sets a moderate gallop and one or two hold-up types track close enough to pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: With a measured tempo in a small six-runner field, the race will compress into a sprint from two furlongs out and the horse best positioned just off the pace will have first use of the rail and room to quicken on the Good to Firm ground. Guest House and Okiru both have the form to track and quicken, and Guest House's strong Yarmouth-going profile (8 runs on Good, 1W3P) makes this shape particularly relevant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Daretobedifferent, handed a soft lead with zero pressure, dictates at a crawl and the field is unable to close from behind in the straight.
scenarios.body: A lone horse setting a walk-then-sprint on a flat track can easily steal enough momentum to hold on if the hold-up horses are caught flat-footed from deep, which is a genuine risk when all rivals are true closers with below-average pace scores. Daretobedifferent has a win on Good going and, despite being racing out of natural role, could exploit the complete absence of pace pressure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a genuine hold-up runner produces a finishing burst from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Daretobedifferent to set a genuinely strong gallop, which contradicts the redistribution context, but if the pace is honest, horses with natural hold-up ability like Okiru or Melting Snow could finish powerfully through tired rivals. Okiru's second on Good to Firm over 7f and Melting Snow's hood and recent run suggest they can sustain a late run if the fractions suit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Scrappy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches, traffic problems develop in the straight and an unfancied runner emerges from the pack.
scenarios.body: A tight six-runner field with several runners mapped away from natural positions can produce an untidy finish where a low-weighted runner like Esdaile or Bellini Spirit sneaks into frame amid positional chaos. This is a low-probability scenario but the compressed field on a flat track does not eliminate the risk of crowding and interference.

watchPoints.text: Guest House and Okiru — if either secures a tracking position two or three lengths off Daretobedifferent in the first half-mile, the compressed straight at Yarmouth gives them a decisive first-mover advantage in the sprint finish.

Daretobedifferent's redistribution to the lead is a pace construction assumption — if the horse drops back to its natural position early, this race has no genuine pace-setter and the tempo could become farcically slow, scrambling all scenario probabilities.

Melting Snow (hood, Ed Dunlop) and Bellini Spirit (86-day break, yard in form) are both wildcards whose market moves at the track should be watched; significant support for either would suggest connections expect a step forward that the bare form does not show.

Yarmouth's 4:08 race is confirmed Good to Firm by the going report — no going change risk — but the flat, straight 1m track plays directly into the hands of horses that can quicken sharply off a slow pace rather than grinders who need strong fractions to deliver their best.

runners_data.name: Cuban Girl
runners_data.note: Trainer Brian Toomey has a poor 14-day return (0/1) and this mare's natural hold-up style means she is here placed artificially on the lead — her true form shows rear-division finishing (6th, 9th, 10th in recent starts), and racing prominently in this way significantly discounts her win chance; 36 days off is not a notable concern.

runners_data.name: The Ubermensch
runners_data.note: Consistent in form (6-4-3-2-1 recent sequence) with a win over this exact 12f course and going combination and a placed effort over 10f on Good to Firm equivalent — Billy Loughnane is a sharp jockey for Michael Bell who has a solid 1/22 14-day return, and the trip and surface are squarely in his favour.

runners_data.name: Risen Again
runners_data.note: John & Rhys Flint in excellent 14-day form (3/8), but Risen Again's recent form reads 6-0-0-6-6, suggesting significant handicap regression; true hold-up style means he is squeezed into a midfield mapping role he hasn't earned on merit, and 59 days off adds a further question mark at this level.

runners_data.name: Big Alex Walmsley
runners_data.note: Benoit de la Sayette takes the ride for Mrs I G-Leveque (0/2 in 14 days), and the horse's record shows he is still searching for a win (0W in his history), with his best effort a single placing over 8f on Good going; genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield by field congestion, and the step up to 1m2f on Good to Firm is an unknown.

runners_data.name: Nuptown Girl
runners_data.note: Ian Williams is a volume trainer with a 3/38 14-day strike rate, and Nuptown Girl arrives fresh (5 days since last run) with strong course-trip form — a win over 12f on Good, two places over 10f on Good, and a consistent string of form figures (3-5-4-1-4-2); Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim is a meaningful weight concession in a tight confined handicap.

races.paceDynamic: Cuban Girl is redistributed to the lead having a natural hold-up style, meaning this 1m2f contest at Yarmouth will be run at a sustainable, unforced gallop with no genuine front-runner pressing the pace from the gates. The going report consistently clocks this race at Good to Firm, rewarding those who travel smoothly and finish strongly rather than those who grind it out from the front. With Cuban Girl effectively pace-making out of role, and Risen Again, Big Alex Walmsley, and Nuptown Girl all true hold-up types shuffled into midfield by the map because the field is saturated with closers, the tactical picture is compressed — this field holds more hold-up horses than can all successfully deploy late runs from the rear, and the one most likely to actually secure any prominent berth is Nuptown Girl given her course-distance form profile. The race shape strongly favours a horse who can travel mid-to-rear, make smooth headway on the Good to Firm ground, and produce a sustained finish — rewarding genuine hold-up types who find clean air, with The Ubermensch's recent course-distance win and consistent form in this trip range making him the standout beneficiary of that profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ubermensch Controls Late
scenarios.trigger: If Cuban Girl sets a modest uncontested gallop and the field strings out gently, allowing The Ubermensch to travel comfortably and produce his trademark late challenge.
scenarios.body: The Ubermensch has won over 12f on Good and placed over 10f on Good to Firm-similar surfaces, making him ideally suited to this trip and going on a soporific pace; Billy Loughnane can hold his position and deliver him on a smooth run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Nuptown Girl Swoops Wide
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough that a well-timed wide run off the turn delivers a sustained finish before others get organised.
scenarios.body: Nuptown Girl has won over 12f on Good and placed multiple times at this trip, and Ryan Kavanagh's claim gives a weight advantage that could prove decisive in a tight handicap finish; she is a genuine hold-up type whose form figures are improving and who handles this ground well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Cuban Girl struggles to maintain a rhythm out of her natural hold-up role, causing the early gallop to stall and the race to develop into a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: In a compressed dash to the line from the two-furlong pole, the lightest-weighted hold-up types with the sharpest turn of foot benefit most; Nuptown Girl and Big Alex Walmsley both carry less weight and have shown flashes of acceleration at shorter trips.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Logjam, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the glut of true closers all get blocked and Cuban Girl, running free out of role, is left alone to dictate and steal a march on the field.
scenarios.body: Cuban Girl would need to convert her enforced front-running into a stamina-based breakaway, which cuts against her natural style and makes this a low-probability outcome; only a deeply tactical mis-ride by the chasing pack makes this feasible.

watchPoints.text: Watch The Ubermensch's position at halfway — if Billy Loughnane can secure a clean run on the inner without getting bottled behind the cluster of hold-up types, he is the horse most likely to dominate this scenario.
Nuptown Girl's very short turnaround (5 days) could mean she is held together tactically today rather than delivered for a full effort — watch whether Kavanagh rides her for place money early.

Cuban Girl racing on the lead from a hold-up draw and style is a significant flag — if she overdoes the early fractions in an unfamiliar role, she risks weakening rapidly in the final two furlongs and taking runners around her wide.

With four genuine hold-up types compressed into the rear and midfield, traffic management in the straight is a major risk — watch for Ryan Kavanagh (Nuptown Girl) going wide early to avoid the inevitable wall of horses.

The going report consistently stamps this race as Good to Firm despite the headline Good description — any horse with a going concern on fast ground should be downgraded, and Risen Again's soft-ground placing on the stat sheet is worth noting against him here.

races.paceDynamic: Papa Don't Preach is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 5f sprint and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will dictate a sustainable, uncontested pace from the gates. The remainder of the field — Dragon God, Mart, Antiphon, Regal Guest, Nad Alshiba Snow and Surprise Again — are all natural hold-up or midfield types who will be chasing from off the pace. The field holds considerably more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Regal Guest, Antiphon, Nad Alshiba Snow and Surprise Again are all true come-from-behind operators redistributed to midfield, meaning Dragon God and Mart are most likely to secure the closest realistic tracking positions. With a lone, uncontested leader able to control tempo on Good to Firm ground over a tight 5f, this race shape emphatically favours prominent-to-midfield closers with proven form at the trip — particularly those who can sit second or third and sprint past a leader who has had it too easy early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Papa Don't Preach dictates an unchallenged, metronomic gallop and the hold-up horses fail to close the gap over 5f.
scenarios.body: Papa Don't Preach controls every yard from the front, setting a measured pace that is neither slow enough to invite a sprint finish nor fast enough to exhaust herself, and her rivals — having given her first run — find the distance simply too short to reel her in on quick ground. Prominent types who tracked her closely are best placed to benefit if she ties up late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Burst Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and the hold-up horses find the gaps to deliver sustained late runs.
scenarios.body: A true gallop from Papa Don't Preach stretches the field early, but Dragon God and Mart — the horses most naturally placed to track from second or third — conserve enough energy to swoop past a tiring leader inside the final furlong. Genuine hold-up types who get a clean run on fast ground can also arrive late, though the 5f trip is tight for those stuck widest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Papa Don't Preach sets too slow a tempo, bunching the field and creating a sprint-finish lottery from 2f out.
scenarios.body: A crawl from the front turns this into a dash from the two-furlong pole, negating any positional advantage and bringing the entire field into play off a standing sprint. Horses with the highest raw speed figures — regardless of drawn position — are most likely to benefit, and redistributed hold-up types with strong TS figures get a rare chance to express themselves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stops, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Papa Don't Preach sets a fierce pace, overcooks it, and fades sharply in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A blazing early gallop from Papa Don't Preach burns herself out, and the horses sitting closest in second or third position inherit the lead with momentum, holding off any wider closers who have ground to make up. Dragon God's proven 5f form on Good ground makes him the primary beneficiary of this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch Papa Don't Preach's opening furlong split — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable clip, her control of the race from the front makes her extremely difficult to peg back over 5f on Good to Firm ground.

Dragon God is the horse most likely to threaten from the chasing pack given his back-to-back 5f Good-ground placings; watch whether Tom Marquand is able to slot him into second or third early and whether he gets a clear run into the final furlong.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types — Antiphon, Regal Guest, Nad Alshiba Snow and Surprise Again — risk interfering with each other in the rear, creating traffic congestion that could turn a competitive finish into a one-horse race for Papa Don't Preach.

Silvestre De Sousa's booking on Regal Guest stands out in terms of jockey quality relative to the rest of the field — watch whether he attempts to overcome the horse's positional disadvantage with an aggressive positive ride rather than the hold-up style the horse naturally prefers.

Both Antiphon and Surprise Again carry "fades in finish" tags alongside their redistribution flags — if the pace is genuine, these two are the most likely to get outpaced and drop away approaching the final furlong, opening the rail for any horse tracking the leader.
